# Research eligibility: Python, Merchant and customer receiving

This is the customer and automation entry point for the original Research
eligibility workflow. Protocols, source occurrences, named decisions,
resolutions, report links and applications remain in the same immutable dossier.
The browser, JavaScript client, Python client, Merchant tools and exported
customer files all address that dossier.

The complete method and each action's data are documented in
[ELIGIBILITY_REVIEW.md](../research-dossiers/ELIGIBILITY_REVIEW.md). Typed
JavaScript consumers use
[eligibility-consumer.d.mts](../research-dossiers/eligibility-consumer.d.mts).
The Python implementation uses the installed original Node engine, Python
standard library and the existing Research call journal.

## Open the installed workspace

Start or open the existing Research product through Applications or its
`research-workspace` command. Keep its directory, connection file and provider
source configurations in their original private locations. The Python client
borrows that listener:

~~~python
from stellar_forge_buyer.research_workspace import ResearchWorkspace

with ResearchWorkspace(
    checkout="/absolute/source-checkout",
    connection_file="/absolute/private/research-connection.json",
    directory="/absolute/private/python-client",
    node="node",
) as workspace:
    review = workspace.eligibility("d_ORIGINAL-DOSSIER-UUID")
    page = review.read(section="reviews")
    print(page["dossier"], page["items"])
~~~

The placeholder dossier ID above must be replaced with an ID returned by the
original workspace. The client directory contains the actual bound workspace
identity and complete request attempts. Reopen it to recover a pending call.

Closing this client detaches its requests; it leaves the Research listener
running. It creates no provider task, purchase, session authority or second
review database.

## Read source occurrences and retain the selected revision

`read` supports overview, reviews, occurrences, queue, decisions, resolutions,
studies, impact and operations. A review selects its original question.
A work-set ID further selects its saved protocol and report assignment.

Before a review exists, read occurrences and explicitly select rows belonging
to the intended question:

~~~python
rows = list(review.iter_rows(section="occurrences"))
chosen = [row for row in rows if row["questionId"] == question_id]
~~~

Each row contains its original occurrence ID, edition, question, provider,
source-byte SHA-256, source byte count and normalized content digest. Repeated
DOIs in different questions or editions remain distinct occurrences.

The first page supplies its dossier revision. `iter_rows` retains that
revision for every subsequent page. A manual page with a nonzero offset must
supply the same revision. The native page limit is 100.

~~~python
page = review.read(section="queue", review_id=review_id, limit=30)
while True:
    consume(page["items"])
    if page["nextOffset"] is None:
        break
    page = review.read(
        section="queue", review_id=review_id,
        revision=page["dossier"]["revision"],
        offset=page["nextOffset"], limit=30,
    )
~~~

The overview's units distinguish distinct report occurrences, explicit study
groups, assignments in overlapping work sets, corrected decisions and repeated
applications. Preserve these labels in exported summaries.

## Prepare, inspect and submit a complete action

A command contains one original request ID, observed revision, named actor,
action and complete data object. All actions after create-review include the
review ID. The client validates its outer request with the installed original
parser; the original engine validates action data against saved sources,
protocols and current decisions at commit.

The operator can save and inspect the complete request before sending:

~~~python
prepared = review.prepare(
    "create-workset",
    {
        "protocolId": protocol_id,
        "name": "Retained reports for this scope",
        "occurrenceIds": occurrence_ids,
        "reason": "Selected the original reports under the recorded question.",
    },
    review_id=review_id,
    actor={"id": operator_id, "name": operator_name},
    request_id=request_id,
    expected_revision=observed_revision,
)
review.save_prepared(prepared, "/absolute/private/workset-request.json")
result = review.submit_prepared(prepared)
work_set_id = result["operation"]["result"]["workSet"]["id"]
~~~

This preparation is available to the same operator who submits the action.
The selected protocol determines reviewer assignments and minimum decision
counts. There is no additional client approval step.

The convenience methods accept the exact native data object plus
`request_id`, `expected_revision`, `actor`, and (except create-review)
`review_id`:

| Python method | Original action | Data retained |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create_review | create-review | Question ID, name, description and complete protocol |
| revise_protocol | revise-protocol | Complete next protocol and reason |
| create_workset | create-workset | Protocol ID, name, exact occurrence IDs and reason |
| decide | decide | Work set, report, stage, disposition, criteria, basis, reason and optional prior decision ID |
| resolve | resolve | Every current decision ID, method, disposition and reason |
| study_link | study-link | Explicit report membership and retained source evidence for each report |
| apply_outcomes | apply-outcomes | Explicit report/resolution pairs and optional classification/note changes |
| review_impact | review-impact | Original impact ID, disposition, reason and optional receiving work set |

The current operation ID, review ID and saved child IDs come from
`result["operation"]`. Use those actual results. The consumer verifies the
complete saved request, request hash, operation hash, original and resulting
revisions, actor and dossier before accepting a successful response.

### Decisions and corrections

A decision's actor must match a named reviewer assigned to that stage. An
include/exclude decision supplies all of the stage's criterion answers. An
available basis identifies retained occurrences and a source locator. A
full-text stage requires an available retained basis for a decisive outcome.

A correction supplies the exact prior decision ID in `supersedes`. The
previous decision remains in history, and any resolution using it becomes
stale. Read the resulting queue to obtain the complete current decision ID
set before resolving again.

`unavailable` and `uncertain` preserve the actual information gap. They do
not become exclusion by implication. An adjudication and a consensus are
separately recorded methods.

### Study identities and selected outcomes

Study membership uses the operator's explicit retained-source evidence.
Repeated report metadata alone does not establish that two different reports
describe the same study. Record the actual locators and relationship used.

An applied outcome selects an explicit occurrence/resolution pair. Including
a report requires the final stage to have a current inclusion. The original
supports/contradicts/background classification and existing note remain
unchanged unless supplied in that action.

Later source editions, changed question wording, protocol editions, corrected
resolutions and manual selection changes remain available in the impact view.
Create the required work set and decisions, then record the actual impact
disposition.

## Recover an interrupted request

The Python workspace saves the entire original action before invoking Node.
If the response is lost, use the same client directory:

~~~python
record = review.saved_request(request_id)
result = review.recover(request_id)
~~~

The original engine reconciles the unchanged request before applying its
current-revision check. It returns the saved operation with
`duplicate: true` after a committed-response loss. The dossier metadata in
that reply may be newer than the operation; the saved operation remains bound
to its original revision.

A changed payload cannot reuse the request ID. An ordinary conflict with an
unrelated new dossier revision needs a fresh read, deliberate changes and a
new request ID. Recovery never silently updates an actor, revision, protocol,
report selection or decision set.

Prepared envelopes are bound to the sender workspace. After an independent
customer receiving, select the receiver's actual identity and current
revision for new work. A deliberately repeated historical request can be
submitted as its original request object to demonstrate native replay; an old
sender's prepared workspace envelope is not retargeted.

The JSON export contains the complete selected review projection and
operations. CSV exports a selected queue, decision, resolution, study, impact,
operation or occurrence table. Nested source fields remain JSON cells.

~~~python
with review.export(

    review_id=review_id, revision=selected_revision,

    consume_bytes(source.read())

review.export(

    format="csv", section="decisions",

~~~

Choose one revision for a multi-file report. Omitting revision on an individual

## Build a complete customer delivery

A delivery selection freezes the original metadata, complete revision list,
overview and every selected review section. It exports twelve complete files:

- Original dossier JSON and gzip, containing every saved revision and source blob.
- The normal HTML and Markdown dossier reports.
- The complete eligibility JSON report.
- Seven CSV tables: queue, decisions, resolutions, studies, impact, operations

manifest = delivery.export(review)
manifest = delivery.verify()

An existing delivery directory keeps its first selection. A new selection uses

overwriting it. Portable file recovery uses the original cold reader;
deterministic reports are compared against the same pinned source revision.

All files keep their actual content hashes and counts. Connection tokens,
client configuration files and host directories are outside the delivery.

### Interruption and cancellation

**Reopen this exact capture** first reads the original Analysis job ID. If the
first POST was accepted, it joins that job. A completed job reopens its saved
source and receipt. An interrupted, failed or locally cancelled capture can
explicitly continue through the original start API with the unchanged request.

A completed native pre-admission rejection plus an absent original job is
shown as `NOT_STARTED`. The operator can keep that request in the browser for
inspection or begin a new review with the current source revision. A lost HTTP
reply retains the same request until its original job is reconciled.

**Cancel this local capture** cancels the client and local capture activity.
The original Research application continues to own its purchases and provider
jobs. If source registration already completed, that authoritative source is
retained and is found by the same capture on reopen.

Capture recovery looks for the matching original registered source **before**
opening a Research connection. This also recovers a capture whose source
registration completed just before its Analysis result reply was lost. A
portable restore includes that source and the original job request, so it can
finish the same registration recovery with the provider offline.

The original workspace close cancels active local Research calls, waits for
their cleanup and result publication, then drains its existing Analysis executor.
A source staging copy is removed after verified original registration; its
complete retained source remains under the existing source-document owner.

# Source meanings in the Python customer workspace

The original SF88/SF100 dataset customer retains the reviewed source dictionary alongside the acquired rows. Python can open the dictionary, import the same complete delivery into the existing SQLite database, show definitions beside reviewed SQL aliases, and carry the original source meaning into saved analysis, complete query exports, reports and workbooks.

This is the shared customer continuation of [the CKAN semantic workflow](../../sf30-seller-sdk/ckan/SEMANTIC_WORKFLOW.md) and the [original OData source product](../../sf30-seller-sdk/odata/). The existing acquisition, dataset delivery, SQLite, query, report and workbook engines remain the operating path. The full maintained Python component supplies the new module; there is no new runtime dependency or database service.

## Preserve the producer's source meaning

The receiving engine recognizes two versioned semantic documents. Their original identities, complete physical schema, selected fields and retained source must agree before the existing customer import can run.

| Producer document | Required source contract | Original SF88 semantic response header |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stellar-forge.ckan-semantics.v1 | Retained CKAN capture and reviewed field/CSVW projection | x-ckan-semantics-sha256 |
| stellar-forge.odata-semantics.v1 | provider odata4, protocolVersion 4.0 or 4.01, service and schema URLs, entity container/set/type, retained CSDL schema and capture digests | x-dataset-semantics-sha256 |

Both use the existing semantics query parameter and x-dataset-snapshot response header. A retained response's selected semantic header must match its body; another recognized semantic header, when present, must agree too. Every page retains the same reviewed meaning, source snapshot and original request/query chain. These producer document names are separate from the receiving format: an original completed SF88 session is SF88_SESSION, while an already finalized direct SF100 room is SF100_SCAN.

The shared Python helper API remains read_delivery_semantics, sql_descriptor, sql_context and same_json. A warehouse or native host composes these original helpers and preserves the document unchanged. It does not need a second provider parser or another semantic validation format.

### OData values and presence states

The original OData publisher exposes each selected source property as an ordered physical pair. The dictionary explicitly joins the value column's stateColumn to the state column, and the state column's valueColumn back to the value. Both retain the same sourceField. The state column is a required string with exactly the declared source-presence states value, null and missing.

| Physical field in the retained Northwind Orders projection | Original source meaning |
| --- | --- |
| OrderID | The reviewed value representation of the CSDL OrderID property; sourceDefinition retains the Edm.Int32 type and original entity-key declaration. |
| OrderID_state | Whether OrderID was present with a value, present as null, or absent from the original source record. Its sourceDefinition carries role source-presence and sourcePath OrderID. |
| Freight | The reviewed representation of the original Freight property, with its CSDL type and encoding retained. |
| Freight_state | The source-presence state for Freight, independent of the physical value representation. |

The receiving engine validates those reciprocal pair links and the states actually present in every selected page. Keep the state field when a downstream consumer needs to distinguish an absent property from an explicit source null. A blank physical string can represent an original source null or missing value under the reviewed projection; read the state field instead of inferring source presence from that string.

sourceDefinition describes the original CSDL property, including its type, key membership, nullability and retained facets. projectedDefinition describes the physical customer field. Those two nullability/type descriptions can differ because the publisher preserves source presence and source values through explicit encodings. Inspect encoding and sourceDefinition before choosing calculations. Decimal and Int64 values that the producer preserves as exact text remain exact text in the receiver; structured values encoded as JSON text retain that reviewed representation. The receiver does not silently coerce them to a floating-point number.

The published primary key names value columns. SQL aliases map those physical columns to the reviewed destination names, and the original SQL descriptor states whether the complete key was selected. State columns do not become extra entity keys. Source key declarations remain descriptive; the original immutable-import table does not create an unreviewed uniqueness constraint.

A selected SQL alias changes the SQL name while preserving the dictionary's original published name, sourceField and meaning. For example, mapping OrderID to order_id leaves OrderID_state available under its original physical name. The SQL descriptor records OrderID → order_id, and the full dictionary retains the original reciprocal pair.

## Import an immutable SQL edition

The same DatasetDatabase accepts the original SF88 delivery and a verified direct SF100 delivery. Supply the reviewed field-to-SQL mapping through its existing columns argument.

```python

edition = database.import_delivery(
    delivery,
    columns={"observation_id": "observation_key"},

Existing editions without semantic definitions remain valid.

The same manifest and reviewed mapping produce the same version ID on reimport. Changing the source meaning changes the original delivery manifest and therefore its edition identity. A different SQL mapping creates a separately identified edition over the original retained input.

SQLite keeps the existing scalar rules: numeric strings remain text, original booleans are stored as integers with their observed JSON type retained, and timestamp strings keep their spelling and timezone representation. The source dictionary gives those values their reviewed meaning.

The original source-version reader now attaches the verified dictionary to an edition when a query or report reads that edition's physical table. This connects the source definitions with the exact imported data and SQL mapping.

## What the analysis computes

**Source inventory and coverage.** Each edition retains the original service, selected query, traversal status, counts, source archive identity, source licence, and typed-key multiplicity. Stream summaries keep original observation type and unit. Explicit instants, explicit intervals and unresolved times remain different representations.

**Categorical observations.** Counts group declared category observations by their original literal value, state and type. Adjacent-code analysis requires explicit source instants, a unique observation at both instants, and usable states. Coincident observations and source gaps are not silently converted into duration. A differing adjacent code does not establish the exact transition time.

**Numerical observations.** The unchanged scalar source classifier admits declared numeric/count observations with an original JSON-number result, an explicit phenomenon instant, and the original browser's representability conditions. Every excluded row retains its reason in the classification table and all original fields in observations. Groups keep the original stream kind, typed ID, observation type, observed property and unit.

Decimal source strings enter Decimal and Fraction directly. The programme never aggregates binary browser floats. Minimum and maximum retain original source literals. Sum, mean and median have exact rational representations. mean_decimal_34 is separately identified as a mean rounded to 34 significant decimal digits. Different units and implicit MultiDatastream components are never combined.

**Edition comparison.** Matching reuses the original canonical keys and semantic hashes. A key repeated on either side is ambiguous. Keyless occurrences remain unkeyed on their respective sides. Other classifications are same, changed, observedOnlyLeft and observedOnlyRight. Scope compatibility compares the original service, ordered selected stream kind/URL list and observation query. Observed-only records do not establish deletion or insertion at the provider.

**Metadata.** Entity capture phases and source-page counts are reported separately. An end-time update outside a selected observation window can be a metadata difference without changing the observations in that window. Source quality labels remain publisher values and do not become analyst approvals.

The full calculation module accompanies the derived source document, together with every selected intake descriptor. Both original raw source archives and these derived records remain inside the same portable workspace.

## Descriptor contract

The schema is `stellar-forge.analysis-source-document.v1`. The descriptor has
exactly these top-level fields:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.analysis-source-document.v1",
  "title": "Issuer facts from the retained SEC companyfacts edition",
  "format": "json",
  "document": {
    "path": "files/<64 lowercase SHA-256 digits>.json",
    "bytes": 1234,
    "sha256": "<same 64 lowercase SHA-256 digits>",
    "contentType": "application/json"
  },
  "originals": [],
  "provenance": {
    "kind": "public-source",
    "publisher": "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission",
    "capturedAt": "2026-10-11T22:24:01.883557+00:00",
    "sourceUrl": "https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0000320193.json",
    "scope": "The complete retained companyfacts response for this capture",
    "description": "The maintained SEC parser preserves exact fact values as text."
  },
  "complete": true
}
```

The digest and byte values above are placeholders for the actual file identity.
The content-addressed file must exist and match before registration succeeds.

| Field | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Human-readable source label, at most 200 characters. |
| `format` | `json` or `csv`; the document extension matches it. |
| `document` | The exact analytical input file. Its path contains its own SHA-256. |
| `originals` | Up to 32 retained source/evidence files. Each has the same four file fields plus a unique `role` (at most 80 characters), and optional `sourceUrl`. |
| `provenance.kind` | `public-source` or `operator-file`. |
| `provenance.publisher` | The actual publisher or file origin, at most 200 characters. |
| `provenance.capturedAt` | ISO datetime with an explicit UTC offset. |
| `provenance.scope` | What this particular capture covers, at most 500 characters. |
| `provenance.description` | Original coverage limits and interpretation, at most 12,000 characters. |
| `provenance.sourceUrl` | Required for public sources; canonical HTTPS without credentials, query state or fragment. |
| `provenance.transform` | Optional `{name,sourceUrl,sha256}` identifying the actual maintained transformation source. |
| `complete` | Whether the selected source capture is complete within its declared scope. |

A recent-filings response can be complete for its recent-filings scope while
the publisher lists additional historical files. Retain that distinction in
`scope` and `description`. It does not establish whole-history coverage.
Setting `complete:false` carries the original incomplete acknowledgement into
preview, import and reports.

Original evidence files may use `.json`, `.csv`, `.txt` or `.bin`. The
content type describes the actual bytes. The descriptor is at most 1 MiB;
JSON analysis input at most 32 MiB; an original evidence file at most 32 MiB;
the sum of distinct payload files at most 256 MiB. These are the existing
reader's working limits. Select another genuine source scope when larger
inputs require it.

  --sql 'SELECT SUM(units) AS available_units FROM inventory WHERE available = ?' \
  --parameters '[1]'
```

## Transactions, identity and version selection

`import_delivery()` verifies the original manifest and JSONL through the
existing `DatasetDelivery` file interface. It streams the same verified JSONL
descriptor into one SQLite transaction, checks every row against the original
projected fields, and verifies the final byte count, row count and digest
before commit. A failure or interruption rolls back that table and its
metadata; previously imported versions and named views stay usable.

Each immutable version is identified by the original manifest digest,
SF88 `sourceBindingSha256` and explicit SQL column mapping. The database retains
the exact original manifest, including its dataset snapshot, filters, range
selection, original query hashes, source-page identities and output digests.
Reimporting that same delivery and mapping returns `import_status="UNCHANGED"`
without inserting rows again. Importing a different delivery or mapping creates
another table and leaves current views alone.

`activate(name, version_id, expected_revision=...)` changes the view and records
its selection in one transaction. A first view has revision zero before
selection. A stale revision raises `DATASET_SQL_VIEW_CHANGED`; inspect
`current(name)` and make the selection against that displayed state. Selecting
the already current version at its current revision returns `UNCHANGED` without
incrementing the revision. Any retained version can be selected again with the
same operation. The current version, older tables and activation history remain
in the database across process restarts.

Use `versions(before=..., limit=...)` to page through retained versions, and
`version(version_id)` or `manifest(version_id)` to inspect a particular one.
`next_before` is the stable sequence cursor for the next history page. The
`sf_dataset_activations` table is available to ordinary SQL queries for selection
history. This history records local data selection; original settlement
records continue to belong to the native buyer and accounting engines.

## Value and query behavior

The importer binds the original JSON scalars without column affinity conversion.
Strings remain text, including leading zeros and precise decimal strings;
integers remain signed 64-bit integers, finite JSON numbers remain SQLite numeric
values, and null remains null. Booleans use SQLite's conventional zero/one
representation. Each column's observed JSON types are retained beside the
source-to-SQL name mapping. JSON integers outside SQLite's signed 64-bit range,
non-finite numbers and compound values are rejected without changing the database.
This follows SQLite's documented [storage classes and affinity rules](https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html).

Column names are quoted. If original names collide under SQLite's identifier
comparison or use `_sf_row_number`, supply an explicit mapping:

```python
version = database.import_delivery(
    delivery,
    columns={"Units": "reported_units", "units": "available_units"},
)
```

`_sf_row_number` retains acquired row order and starts at one. Use an explicit
`ORDER BY` when row order matters. Each version reports its physical table name,
so SQL can join or compare retained versions while the application continues to
use a stable named view. The source manifest remains unchanged by SQL naming.

`query()` uses a read-only connection, bound parameters and a SQLite authorizer
that excludes writes, attachment of other databases and extension loading. It
returns `QueryResult(columns, rows, truncated)`. Default limits are 1,000 result
rows, 16 MiB of returned scalar data and ten seconds; callers can select up to
100,000 rows, 256 MiB (`max_result_bytes`) and 300 seconds. Results are collected
incrementally. The `truncated` flag is true if another row would exceed the
selected row or byte limit. SQLite's per-value/row length limit is 16 MiB.
`dictionaries()` requires unique result names;
use SQL aliases for otherwise duplicate names. The original ordered tuple rows
are always available. SQL is evaluated by the same native engine documented by
[Python's sqlite3 interface](https://docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html).

the imported rows. Use native backup for a consistent copy during active work.

writer behavior: a WAL writer can commit while the reader keeps its prior
snapshot; rollback-journal writers wait for that reader to close.

`queryComplete` describes completion of this SQL statement. The statement,
including any explicit SQL `LIMIT`, stays in the manifest. `binding.sourceVersions`
retains the original imported records, their source scope and original payment

```sh

SQLite retains integers, text, nulls, floats and BLOBs without column-affinity
conversion. Use `ORDER BY _sf_export_row` to reproduce the original query's row
order. `export_metadata` binds that result to its manifest's query/source identity.
Use explicit SQL aliases for duplicate column names, names differing only in
case, or a column named `_sf_export_row`.

JSONL uses ordinary scalar values. BLOBs use `{"$sqliteBlob":"BASE64"}` and
non-finite floats use `{"$sqliteFloat":"Infinity"}` (or `-Infinity`/`NaN`).
`QueryExport.rows()` decodes these values. Large integers remain exact Python
integers. Consumers whose JSON parser rounds large integers should use the
SQLite output or an exact-integer JSON parser.

CSV uses an empty field for SQL null and `base64:` for binary values; JSONL and
SQLite preserve the distinction between null and empty text. By default,
formula-like text and headers receive an apostrophe prefix for spreadsheet
import. `--literal-csv` retains their literal text instead. The manifest records
which setting was used. Exact decimal text remains text in JSONL and SQLite;
spreadsheet software's import settings control its conversion of CSV cells.

## Application streaming, progress and cancellation

```python
from threading import Event
from stellar_forge_buyer.sqlite_dataset import DatasetDatabase

source = DatasetDatabase("/private/customer-analysis", create=False)
reviewed_views = source.view_bindings()
cancelled = Event()

with source.stream_query(
    "SELECT sku, quantity FROM inventory ORDER BY sku",
    expected_views=reviewed_views,
    cancel=cancelled.is_set,
) as rows:
    for record in rows.dictionaries():
        process_inventory_row(record)
    print(rows.rows_read, rows.complete)

result = source.export_query(
    "SELECT sku, quantity FROM inventory ORDER BY sku",
    destination="/private/customer-exports/application-export",
    expected_views=reviewed_views,
    cancel=cancelled.is_set,
    progress=lambda state: update_job_progress(state),
)
```

Use the streaming context manager so early exit releases the cursor and read
transaction. `complete` becomes true only after exhausting the cursor. Progress
reports arrive every 4096 rows and after publication; a host can call
`cancelled.set()` from its cancellation handler. The original SQLite VM progress
handler also interrupts expensive SQL before it returns a row.

Exports create their destination exclusively, write private temporary outputs,
flush complete data, then publish the manifest last. All files use mode `0600`
and directories `0700`. Cancellation and ordinary errors remove this operation's
incomplete output files. An abrupt process kill can leave an incomplete directory;
opening it reports `QUERY_EXPORT_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE_OR_INCOMPLETE`. A completed
manifest survives a lost final reply or a failed final progress callback and can
be reopened. A new export never overwrites an existing destination.

## Cell mappings

| Mapping | Input and Excel representation |
| --- | --- |
| Native value | Original text stays literal text. Integers and finite numbers fit into Excel numeric cells when the precision policy permits. Binary and nonfinite values have explicit text representations. |
| Text | Keeps a textual representation, including leading zeros and strings beginning with `=`. |
| Integer | Accepts an original integer or an integer string. Values beyond 15 digits remain text with **Preserve**. |
| Number | Accepts a finite number or decimal string. **Preserve** retains values beyond Excel numeric precision or range as text. |
| Decimal text | Validates a finite decimal and keeps its exact original spelling and scale, including `599.010000`. |
| Boolean | Accepts a boolean, integer `0`/`1`, or text `true`/`false`. |
| ISO date | Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD`. Dates before 1900 remain text. |
| Timestamp → UTC | Requires an ISO timestamp with a timezone, converts supported values to UTC, and labels the Excel format UTC. |
| Local timestamp | Requires an ISO timestamp without a timezone. |
| Binary → Base64 | Encodes original binary bytes as Base64 text. |

**Preserve** is the default numeric choice. **Use Excel numeric precision** is an
explicit choice to write numeric cells with Excel's precision. Use **Decimal
text** for amounts whose original decimal scale is part of the deliverable.

Each column chooses an empty Excel cell or a text label for SQL null. The
default label is `NULL`. Excel can display an empty source string and an empty
cell alike; their original values and types remain in the included query JSONL
or published report JSON. The manifest also counts null, empty-string and
precision conversions for every output column.

The writer uses ISO date storage with the 1900 date system. Dates before 1900
and timestamps containing precision beyond milliseconds remain original text.
All strings are explicitly written as literal strings; formula text is retained
as data. Text exceeding Excel's 32,767 UTF-16-unit cell limit or containing
unsupported XML characters ends the job with a specific cell error.

Every worksheet supports 16,384 selected columns and 1,048,575 data rows plus
its header. Larger results continue on numbered worksheets. The writer checks
all final sheet names for collisions, including continuation sheets and the
reserved `Readme` and `Sources` sheets.

[
  {"source": "amount", "source_index": 0, "header": "Principal", "type": "decimal-text"},
  {"source": "amount", "source_index": 1, "header": "Fee", "type": "decimal-text"}
]
```

A unique report label can still be selected by name. An ambiguous repeated
label requires its position, and a changed label at that position produces a
source error. Query-export recipes continue selecting their original named
columns.

The saved definition contains those bindings. Later changes to current views,
saved SQL or other reports leave the selected retained results available. A
changed source manifest or original report digest produces a source error.

## Headless customer delivery

`WorkspaceWorkbookClient` uses the current private launch record of the existing
workspace. It saves a definition, builds it, streams all three customer files,
receives the handoff and reopens the original typed sources.

Create a private recipe. Source IDs and digests come from the Workbooks picker
or its source API; use actual retained values in place of the example labels:

```json
{
  "name": "customer_operations",
  "expected_revision": 0,
  "title": "Customer operations",
  "notes": "Complete retained sales summary for the selected period.",
  "sheets": [{
    "name": "Sales summary",
    "source": {
      "kind": "query-export",
      "id": "EXISTING_32_CHARACTER_EXPORT_ID",
      "sha256": "EXISTING_64_CHARACTER_MANIFEST_SHA256"
    },
    "columns": [
      {"source": "region", "header": "Region", "type": "text"},
      {"source": "total", "header": "Total", "type": "decimal-text"}
    ]
  }]
}
```

```sh
chmod 600 /private/customer/workbook-recipe.json
stellar-forge-workbook-deliver \
  --database /private/customer/database \
  --recipe /private/customer/workbook-recipe.json \
  --operation /private/customer/workbook-delivery
```

The operation directory retains the exact save request and build ID before the
HTTP writes. Run the same command with the same recipe and operation directory
to recover a lost reply or interrupted client. The server returns the same
saved definition and workbook job. Completed files are reused after their byte
counts and SHA-256 values match the retained delivery.

The Python API is also available:

```python
from stellar_forge_buyer.workbook_client import WorkspaceWorkbookClient

client = WorkspaceWorkbookClient("/private/customer/database")
delivery = client.deliver(recipe, "/private/customer/workbook-delivery")
