## Offline receiving and reopening

The handoff contains `workbook.xlsx`, `definition.json`, `manifest.json` and the
original source exports under `sources/`. The manifest binds their exact bytes
and records the completed row counts, physical worksheet names and mappings.

```sh
stellar-forge-workbook receive \
  --archive /private/inbox/handoff.zip \
  --sha256 EXPECTED_HANDOFF_SHA256 \
  --destination /private/inbox/customer-workbook

stellar-forge-workbook inspect \
  --delivery /private/inbox/customer-workbook \
  --manifest-sha256 EXPECTED_MANIFEST_SHA256

stellar-forge-workbook copy \
  --delivery /private/inbox/customer-workbook \
  --destination /private/customer/archive/workbook-edition-1
```

Receiving checks the exact member list and hashes while streaming into private
staging tied to the selected destination and archive. After complete inspection,
it atomically publishes the final directory without replacing an existing target.
A process interruption during extraction leaves the final destination absent;
receiving the same archive at the same destination reclaims its own unfinished
staging and completes the original operation. Its default decompressed byte limit is 1 GiB; set
`--max-bytes` to the reviewed size when receiving a larger handoff. Existing
destinations are preserved. Offline inspect and copy use the manifest and
original result files without needing the workbook-writing extra.

## Workspace API

These routes use the existing loopback server and its
`X-Analysis-Capability` header.

| Route | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workbook-sources?kind=query-export&before=SEQUENCE` | Page complete native query exports and their typed source bindings. |
| `GET /api/workbook-sources?kind=report&before=SEQUENCE` | Page published report sections. |
| `POST /api/workbooks/NAME` | Save a definition with `id`, `expected_revision`, title, notes and ordered sheets. |
| `GET /api/workbooks/NAME?revision=N` | Reopen a saved definition, digest and revision history. |
| `GET /api/workbooks/NAME/preview?revision=N&sheet=0` | Preview its saved typed cell projection. |
| `POST /api/start/workbook` | Build with `id`, `name`, `revision` and `definition_sha256`. |
| `GET /api/jobs/ID` | Read the existing job status, progress and complete result. |
| `GET /api/workbook-runs?before=SEQUENCE` | Page retained delivery history. |
| `POST /api/workbook-runs/ID/cancel` | Request cancellation of the selected running workbook. |
| `GET /api/workbook-runs/ID/file?name=workbook.xlsx` | Stream the original Excel file, handoff ZIP or manifest with its exact byte count and SHA-256 header. |

On process restart, the existing job log records interrupted work. The workbook
component adopts a complete retained delivery only after checking the saved
definition, every retained file and the complete ZIP. Interrupted incomplete
work remains visible in the original history; the customer can use a new build
ID for another attempt.

Writer API reference: [openpyxl optimized modes](https://openpyxl.readthedocs.io/en/stable/optimized.html)
and [date and time handling](https://openpyxl.readthedocs.io/en/stable/datetime.html).


## Recurring workbook editions

A recurring workbook keeps the existing workbook name and ordered worksheets
while replacing selected complete source results. Open a saved definition in
**Workbooks**, choose **Review newer sources**, then select the worksheet whose
source you want to update.

The source picker starts from that worksheet's recorded lineage:

- A query-export successor must be a newer complete export with exactly the
  same SQL and typed parameter values. Its title alone does not identify it.
  Saved-query edits need a separate query run and export before they can be
  chosen through the ordinary workbook editor.
- A report successor must be a newer publication of the same saved report and
  saved query. A uniquely occurring query may move to another section. If that
  query occurs more than once, the section position must also match.

**Find newer complete results** reads the retained results. **Older results**
continues the cursor through every eligible completed-result page. The comparison
shows old and new row counts, ordered column labels, added and removed labels,
SQL, typed parameters, bound views and immutable source versions. A newer result
may contain the same rows; the explicit selection records which completed
edition the customer intends to deliver.

### Review the source and column changes

Choose **Use this complete result** for each changed worksheet. The original
headers, formatting, null policy and precision policy remain in the editor.
Columns with a unique old and new label can be mapped by that label. A missing
or duplicate old label requires an explicit choice in **Source column**. Report
columns show their ordinal as well as their label.

For example, an old report might contain:

| Old source column | Workbook header | New source column |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label [0]` | Domain | `domain [1]` |
| `label [1]` | Title | `label [0]` |

Choose each new source column explicitly. The editor cannot determine the
meaning of the two old `label` columns from their names. Added source columns
are available in the same picker; add a worksheet column when you want one in
the delivered workbook. Review its type, null treatment and precision policy
as part of that change.

Use **Keep original source and columns** to restore the selected worksheet.
Other worksheets can keep their prior complete results. Worksheet positions
stay fixed during an edition review so each before/after record has an
unambiguous counterpart. A normal workbook edit can change the worksheet
structure separately.

Add an edition note explaining the reporting period or source change, then
choose **Review selected sources and cells**. The review shows up to 20 actual rows per
worksheet, the projected cells, observed source types and conversion errors.
Correct any displayed mapping or conversion error and review again. This is a
preview: the complete workbook build reads and projects every retained row.
A conversion problem later in the result fails the build with its original
error in delivery history.

Choose **Save workbook definition** after the review is ready. The existing definition
compare-and-swap checks the expected head revision. If another operator has
saved meanwhile, reopen the current definition and review the intended change
against it. The new edition uses the original workbook build, progress,
cancellation, authenticated download and offline receiving controls.

The browser retains the draft review and pending save identity in its existing
workspace-specific local storage. Reconnecting after a lost save reply reuses
the same request. A successful save is a new immutable revision; an existing
revision and its completed delivery remain available through history.

### Headless edition delivery

The same operation is available through the existing client. Obtain the base
definition and its digest, discover the intended successors, and create this
private recipe shape using the actual IDs and mappings from those responses:

```json
{
  "base_revision": 1,
  "definition_sha256": "EXACT_BASE_DEFINITION_SHA256",
  "expected_revision": 1,
  "reason": "October reporting edition; reconcile renamed report columns.",
  "definition": {
    "name": "customer_operations",
    "title": "Customer operations",
    "notes": "Reviewed reporting edition.",
    "sheets": [{
      "name": "Sales summary",
      "source": {
        "kind": "query-export",
        "id": "EXISTING_NEW_COMPLETE_EXPORT_ID",
        "sha256": "EXACT_NEW_SOURCE_MANIFEST_SHA256"
      },
      "columns": [
        {"source": "region", "header": "Region", "type": "text"},
        {"source": "total", "header": "Total", "type": "decimal-text"}
      ]
    }]
  }
}
```

The proposed definition must contain all existing worksheets in their current
order. Include the original source and mapping for every worksheet being kept.
For a report column, include its actual `source` label and numeric
`source_index`; both are checked against the chosen section.

```sh
stellar-forge-workbook-deliver \
  --database /private/customer/database \
  --refresh-recipe /private/customer/october-edition.json \
  --operation /private/customer/october-edition-delivery
```

Or use the Python client:

```python
client = WorkspaceWorkbookClient("/private/customer/database")
delivery = client.refresh(recipe, "/private/customer/october-edition-delivery")
```

The client retains `review.json`, the exact reviewed save request, its stable
request ID and one build ID before sending the save. Run the same command with
the same recipe and operation directory after interruption. It resumes the
same saved edition and build, streams the complete files, verifies the retained
downloads, receives the handoff and writes `delivery.json`. A different recipe
requires a different operation directory.

### Refresh API and replay

| Route | Request or result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workbooks/NAME/refresh?revision=N&sheet=0&limit=25&before=SEQUENCE` | Source lineage, candidate comparisons, suggested mappings, unresolved columns and the next cursor. Omit `before` for the first page. |
| `POST /api/workbooks/NAME/refresh-review` | Recipe above; returns the normalized definition, per-sheet changes, actual cell previews, readiness and `review_sha256`. |
| `POST /api/workbooks/NAME/refresh` | The identical recipe plus a stable 32-character `id` and the returned `review_sha256`; saves through the original definition store. |

The server recomputes the source and mapping review before accepting its
digest. The digest covers the base definition, proposed definition, expected
revision, reason and complete before/after source bindings. Mutable current-head
display information is outside that digest so a reply lost after a committed
save can be recovered with its original request identity. Reusing that identity
for a different change is rejected.

### Complete handoff and historical reopening

A refreshed handoff contains the new Excel workbook, current definition,
complete current sources and the exact predecessor definitions identified by
its refresh history. The prior definitions live at
`history/definition-N.json`. Their complete original sources are retained under
the same `sources/` layout, with a shared source stored once.

Each refresh origin records the base revision and definition digest, the
reviewed change and its reason. The delivery manifest lists the retained
definition history and hashes every included file. Offline inspect follows
the descending history chain and checks each exact definition. A sequence of
refreshes carries that chain back to its original saved definition. An ordinary
manual save starts its own subsequent refresh chain; other saved revisions
remain available in workspace history.

Use a receiver containing this edition feature for these extended handoffs.
Excel itself opens the generated `.xlsx` normally. The original earlier
workbook and archive retain their prior bytes and can still be received or
reopened independently.

# Customer data-analysis workspace

For complete query files beyond an analysis preview, use the **Exports** tab
and the [complete query export workflow](WORKSPACE_EXPORTS.md). It joins the
original reviewed query, native streaming writer, cancellation, retained file
downloads and portable reopen in this same workspace.

Use an acquired dataset in a local browser, keep saved analyses and their actual results, and reopen the complete analytical database after restart. The workspace uses the original Python `DatasetAcquisition`, `DatasetDelivery` and `DatasetDatabase`. It imports completed native deliveries; it does not execute an acquisition or financial operation.

The Data tab selects original deliveries, reviews retained versions and scalar types, downloads the original manifest, and selects the version served by a named SQL view. The Changes tab compares acquired versions, retains complete row/schema differences and applies an explicitly reviewed candidate. The Analysis tab saves parameterized SQL and its revisions, executes it against a reviewed selection, pages retained results and exports JSON or CSV. Activity reopens imports, analyses and consistent database backups.

## Start with a completed original acquisition

Use Python 3.11+ and install this source's Python package beside its matching full native Node runtime. The workspace modules and their browser assets are included by the existing Python package definition; there are no new dependencies.

```sh
python -m pip install --no-deps ./stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli/python

python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer/analysis \
  --checkout /path/to/public-commons-sprint-2026 \
  source --name inventory \
  --session /private/customer/inventory-acquisition \
  --room /private/customer/inventory-data-room

python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer/analysis \
  --checkout /path/to/public-commons-sprint-2026 \
  serve --open
```

Use the existing session produced by [the original dataset application](DATASETS.md). `source` registers its native identity and the hash of its immutable `session.json`. It inspects the original session without running a page. `--room` selects its existing SF100 room; omitting that option chooses a private destination inside this analysis directory. The source alias, exact native paths, source revision and observed acquisition status are saved in the database. The browser uses those declared aliases and does not accept arbitrary source paths.

`serve` binds to `127.0.0.1` and chooses an available port. `--open` opens the private capability link in the local browser. For a remote terminal, read the URL from the private `analysis-launch.json` inside the selected database directory using your existing secure local browser/port-forward setup. The ordinary startup line contains the address and control-file path. Capabilities change at every server launch; open the new private link after restart.

The listener enforces its exact Host and Origin, same-origin browser requests and a capability header for every data operation. It is a local operator application, not an Internet-facing hosted service. Its assets contain no database contents or capability. Python's [HTTP server](https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html) is the local transport.

An already built earlier Python wheel keeps its original source identity. Use a cumulative companion wheel that contains this source, or the source installation above. The workspace's matching Node runtime is needed only when registering or importing original acquisitions.

## Import and select data

1. Select the registered source on **Data**. Choose **Import original delivery**. An incomplete acquisition is rejected; complete sessions are opened through the original native exporter. A previously finalized SF100 room is reused.
2. Inspect the resulting imported version. Its row count, snapshot, table, exact original manifest digest and per-column JSON types remain visible. **Download original manifest** returns the stored original bytes, without JSON re-encoding.
3. Enter a SQL view name such as `inventory` and choose **Select for this view**. The action uses the displayed current revision. A stale selection is rejected without changing the view.
4. Use **Query** beside a current view, or **Query this immutable table** on a selected version, to begin an analysis.

Import does not change an existing SQL view. The exact same native delivery and mapping reuse its existing immutable table. An optional column-mapping JSON object maps original field names to SQL names:

```json
{"units":"available_units"}
```

That creates a separate mapped edition of the same delivery, retaining the original edition. It is not a new merchant snapshot or another purchase. Select its version explicitly before using it through a current view. Each row keeps its original ordering column `_sf_row_number`; scalar handling and identifier rules are described in [SQLITE.md](SQLITE.md).

To select a different native acquisition for an existing source alias, stop this workspace and register it with `source --expected-revision N`. The existing source revision is in Data and in `status`. Re-registering the same paths and immutable session is unchanged. Earlier imported data remains available. Use a different room for a different acquisition; original SF100 identity checks apply when a destination already exists.

## Save and use an analysis

For the original inventory example, whose `available` field is a native Boolean and whose `units` field is an integer:

```sql
SELECT SUM(units) AS available_units, COUNT(*) AS available_skus
FROM inventory
WHERE available = :available;
```

Parameters:

```json
{"available":true}
```

Name the analysis `available_inventory` and choose **Save analysis**. SQL and parameter text are retained as an immutable revision. The editor can load a previous saved revision; its next save uses the current head revision displayed in the editor. Changes made by another client are detected before replacement. Unsaved editor contents are retained in this browser's local draft, and data refresh does not replace them.

**Run analysis** records the exact SQL, parameters and reviewed current-view identities before dispatch. The original `DatasetDatabase.query` reads those view identities and the returned rows in the same SQLite transaction. If a current view changed since review, the operation fails with `DATASET_SQL_VIEWS_CHANGED`. Refresh, review the new selection and run explicitly. SQLite's [transaction isolation](https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html) keeps the accepted query's selection consistent while another client later activates a view.

The retained result includes the actual transaction's view revisions and physical read tables. It remains associated with that execution when views, saved queries or the editor subsequently change. Opening or exporting a result never reruns SQL. Parameter text is parsed by Python, so the browser does not round a signed 64-bit integer parameter before SQLite receives it. Boolean parameters bind as the ordinary SQLite `0`/`1` values.

Default maximum rows is 1,000, adjustable to 100,000. The workspace also limits each query to 4 MiB of returned scalar values and 20 seconds. Results record truncation explicitly. Browser pages contain at most 100 saved rows. Invalid SQL retains its SQLite diagnostic in the failed activity record and leaves previous successful results intact. The original read-only authorizer prohibits database writes, attached databases and file/extension functions.

### Result exports

**JSON** exports ordered columns and native scalar rows, plus the exact executed request, view bindings, read tables and retained result identity. Signed 64-bit integers are emitted as their exact JSON number text. Binary values use an explicit base64 envelope; a non-finite real produced by an SQL expression uses an explicit `sqlite-real` envelope because JSON cannot encode it as a number.

**CSV** exports every retained row, including rows beyond the currently visible browser page, with ordinary CSV quoting and the saved column order. Nulls become empty fields; binary values are base64. The JSON result retains their type information. CSV does not rerun the query and does not infer payment or settlement from data values.

The browser displays typed textual cells so JavaScript does not round large SQLite integers. `result_sha256` identifies the canonical retained typed result, including its original data selection; it is checked when that result is reopened. It is not the hash of the separately formatted JSON or CSV download.

## Review a candidate before changing a current view

The **Changes** tab compares two original imported editions. Use it for a newly acquired snapshot, a different acquired query, or a separately mapped edition. Both source identities remain visible. A narrower category filter can remove rows from an acquired result, and a changed projection can remove a column without changing the source records.

1. Keep the baseline selected for a current SQL view such as `inventory`.
2. Import and select the candidate in Data. Choose **Review changes against a current view** and select the baseline view. The displayed view name, version and revision remain the baseline for this comparison; refresh does not silently replace them.
3. Choose 1–16 SQL columns that uniquely identify each row and are present in both editions, such as `sku` or a composite key. The interface preselects a conventional `id`, `sku` or `record_id` column when present. The complete comparison verifies it: a null or duplicate key rejects the operation with its side and original row number.
4. Choose **Compare every row**. Inspect added rows, removed rows, changed fields and rows whose only difference is position. Open a row to see all baseline and candidate fields with retained scalar types. Missing fields and null values are different. Original filters, ranges, ordering, projected fields, snapshots and manifest identities are shown together.
5. Enter a review note and choose **Select reviewed candidate**. Original view activation and the comparison's selection record commit in the same SQLite transaction using the exact reviewed revision. A changed current view cannot be overwritten by an older comparison; load its current selection and compare again.
6. Choose **Query current view** to continue with the original saved-analysis editor. Existing SQL drafts keep their ordinary discard confirmation, and earlier query results keep their own actual data selection.

Comparison traverses every row in both original immutable SQL tables. It retains all added, removed, changed and order-only records in the original database. Unchanged rows stay in their original tables and contribute to the complete counts and observation hashes. Position changes on rows with changed fields contribute to the separate reordered-row count. Column additions/removals and changes in original JSON type declarations remain visible even when there are no row differences. Browser pages hold at most 50 differences and normally at most 4 MiB of records; one larger complete record is never split.

Matching and field comparison use the original database's typed SQL scalars. Integers and reals remain distinguishable, signed 64-bit integers reach the browser as exact text, and a missing projected column differs from SQL null. The original importer represents JSON Booleans as SQLite `0`/`1`; original JSON type declarations remain in the schema comparison. The comparison does not reconstruct a per-row Boolean distinction that the original SQL representation did not retain.

A comparison has a 120-second execution budget and a 128 MiB budget for retained typed difference records. It either completes every source row or fails and rolls back the report; it never presents a sample or truncated comparison as complete. Difference rows and the COMPLETE activity status share one commit. Restart marks interrupted work explicitly; earlier imported versions and completed comparisons remain usable.

### Retained review exports

**Prepare JSON report** writes the complete report, original edition metadata, exact retained selection (if any) and every typed difference. **Prepare CSV differences** writes one `comparison` metadata row followed by `difference` rows for individual fields. Every CSV row carries comparison/report, baseline/candidate version/manifest and review identities. The metadata row includes the acquired query scopes, counts, schema changes, matching keys and review, so a comparison with zero row differences still carries its source identity. Type columns distinguish missing fields, null, integer, real and string values.

Exports are file-backed and streamed from retained SQLite records. Each request binds the exact completed report and selection. If a report is selected while an older export request is waiting, that request fails instead of silently substituting the new review. A new export action uses the newly displayed review. Activity retains the complete file's path, byte count and SHA-256. Download verifies and streams the same private descriptor. Browsers with the file-save API write the response stream directly; other browsers download files up to 64 MiB, with larger complete files available at their displayed local paths.

The comparison and selected-review records are in the original database backup. Standalone exports are not copied into that database. After recovery, reopen the comparison and prepare its export again: it reproduces the report without a Node runtime, acquisition directory, wallet or network. An older export job retains its original location and cannot download a file from the previous workspace path.

For embedding, `workspace.changes.page(comparison_id)` returns the report, selection, current view and `selection_sha256`. Dispatch a comparison using the original background interface:

```python
import uuid

request = {
    "id": uuid.uuid4().hex,
    "view": "inventory",
    "expected_revision": reviewed_view["revision"],
    "base_version_id": reviewed_view["version_id"],
    "candidate_version_id": candidate["version_id"],
    "keys": ["sku"],
}
job = workspace.start("compare", request)
# Reopen workspace.job(job["id"]) until COMPLETE, FAILED or INTERRUPTED.
# Repeating the same request ID/content returns that original job.
```

After completion, call `workspace.changes.select(job_id, {"id": uuid.uuid4().hex, "result_sha256": report["result_sha256"], "note": "Reviewed category selection"})`. An identical selection request returns its retained result; a different request cannot overwrite it. For an export, pass `comparison_id`, `result_sha256`, the page's `selection_sha256`, `format` (`json` or `csv`) and a new `id` to `start("change-export", request)`. `workspace.changes.history(before=..., limit=25)` and `page(..., kind="removed", after=0)` reopen reports beyond the latest activity page. Start a changed comparison/filter at `after=0`; its returned cursor belongs to that selection.

## Compose and publish a customer report

**Reports** turns saved analyses into an ordered customer document. It uses the
same acquired editions, saved SQL recipes, typed rows and database backup.

1. Save the analyses you need in **Analysis**. A query can be used more than once
   with different effective parameters.
2. Open **Reports**, name the report, and add its title and introduction. Add up
   to twelve sections; select each saved query and its exact revision, write its
   title/context, review the SQL, and set its parameters. Move sections into the
   intended reading order.
3. Save the definition. Query revisions are pinned: later edits in **Analysis**
   do not silently alter this report. **Load current query revision** explicitly
   adopts a changed recipe before the next definition save. Unsaved report
   authoring survives a browser refresh in this workspace's local draft.
4. Review **Current data selection** and run the saved report. All sections use
   one original SQLite read transaction, including their physical tables and
   selected views. A data selection changed before execution requires a fresh
   review. A subsequent selection cannot change the retained result.
5. Inspect each complete table, its original acquisition scope and any original
   comparison decision that selected the working edition. That decision's note,
   original query/projection and comparison/selection IDs follow the report.
6. Add a review/handover note and **Publish this report edition**. This retains a
   named edition inside the private workspace. It does not send it to anyone.
   Competing publication edits compare the current revision; **Refresh report
   state** loads the actual current publication before a new attempt.
7. Prepare **printable HTML**, **complete JSON**, or the **CSV bundle**, then
   download the resulting file. Publication history reopens earlier editions
   independently of later report definitions, data selections and reviews.

A report does not publish a silently shortened query result. If any section
reaches its saved row ceiling, the 4 MiB raw-value ceiling or the original
20-second query deadline, the whole run fails and leaves earlier reports intact.
Choose a more specific query or increase its saved row limit (up to 100,000)
before explicitly adopting that query revision. A complete report allows at most
60 seconds of query work and 32 MiB of encoded table rows. No partial report
becomes a publication.

The HTML is a complete offline document with print styles, typed table values,
narrative, original data scope and query details; it loads no scripts, fonts or
remote assets. JSON contains every table with the same exact integer/string,
NULL and binary encodings used in the analysis workspace. The CSV ZIP contains
one ordinary CSV per section, complete `report.json`, printable `report.html`
and a short index. The original positional columns are preserved even when SQL
uses duplicate column labels. CSV represents both NULL and an empty string as
an empty field; the typed JSON retains their distinction.

Publication/result IDs, original data selection and reviewed source scope remain
inside every complete export. Files are generated and downloaded incrementally;
the browser uses its file-save stream where available and otherwise permits
downloads up to 64 MiB. An export can be up to 128 MiB. The customer decides how
to share the private report. Absolute acquisition and database paths are not
included in its dataset source metadata.

### Use the same report workflow from Python

Use the original `AnalysisWorkspace` while its browser server is closed. Its
existing process lease prevents two workspace job owners from running together.
The following example assumes `available_inventory` revision 1 was already
saved against the customer's imported data:

```python
from uuid import uuid4
from stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace import AnalysisWorkspace

workspace = AnalysisWorkspace("/private/customer/analysis")
try:
    definition = workspace.reports.save("inventory_review", {
        "id": uuid4().hex,
        "expected_revision": 0,
        "title": "Acquired inventory review",
        "introduction": "Review the exact acquired query and selected edition.",
        "sections": [{
            "title": "Available inventory",
            "note": "Availability uses the retained source's declared values.",
            "query_name": "available_inventory",
            "query_revision": 1,
            "parameters_text": '{"available": true}',
        }],
    })
    pinned = workspace.reports.definition(
        definition["name"], revision=definition["revision"])
    job = workspace.start("report", {
        "id": uuid4().hex,
        "name": definition["name"],
        "revision": definition["revision"],
        "definition_sha256": pinned["sha256"],
        "expected_views": workspace.database.view_bindings(),
    })
    # Poll workspace.job(job["id"]) for COMPLETE, then inspect:
    # workspace.reports.result(job["id"], section=0, offset=0)
finally:
    workspace.close()  # waits for its existing background worker
```

`reports.publish(job_id, {id, result_sha256, expected_revision, note})` retains
a reviewed edition. `reports.publications(name=...)` returns its exact
`publication` and `sha256`; pass those to
`workspace.start("report-export", {id, publication_id, publication_sha256,
format})`, where format is `html`, `json`, or `csv`. The original
`report_export_file(export_job_id)` returns the retained file and byte/digest
metadata. `reports.history`, `reports.result`, `reports.definition` and
`reports.publications` reopen the same source, tables and history used by the
browser.

Definition saves, publication requests and background jobs retain their request
IDs. Retry an uncertain request with the same ID and unchanged content; its
original record returns even if today's definition or publication has advanced.
Use a new ID for a deliberate new action. Publication changes never change a SQL
view or start a purchase.

Reports and publications live in the original database backup, including all
typed rows and the source decisions. After restoring that database in a new
private directory, reopen the existing publication and prepare its export again.
This regenerates the same report from retained rows; it does not re-run SQL or
acquire data. Old export jobs retain their original directory identity and
cannot be used to read another workspace's files. The single workspace owner
cleans only its own incomplete `.reports-*` staging files at startup.

## Back up and reopen

Choose **Create database backup**. The original SQLite backup operation creates a consistent copy containing the imported rows, exact original manifests, current views, activation history, registered source descriptions, saved query revisions, complete comparisons and selections, and retained analysis results. The completed action gives its local path, byte count and SHA-256. Files of at most 256 MiB can also be downloaded from the browser; larger backups remain complete at the displayed local path. Download rechecks the recorded digest.

The native backup directory is create-only and unique for that action. To reopen a copied backup, keep its file named `datasets.sqlite3` in a private directory and start the same workspace there:

```sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/restored-analysis \
  serve --open
```

Omit `--checkout` to use retained data and analyses without any Node runtime, source acquisition directory, wallet keys or network access. Old source aliases remain recorded, but imports are disabled in that invocation. Backup copies do not copy external acquisition/room files, native financial state, or previous standalone backup files. Those original products retain their existing recovery mechanisms. A backup captures its own in-progress job record; opening the copied database marks that record interrupted, without replaying it. All committed analytical data and earlier completed results remain usable.

One process owns background work for each analysis database. A second workspace process cannot recover a live process's jobs. An abrupt stop rolls back an incomplete SQLite transaction; on the next open, unfinished work is marked **INTERRUPTED**, and no job is automatically dispatched. If an import committed before its activity record was finalized, explicitly importing the same original delivery reuses the retained version. Completed results are committed atomically with their completion state.

The read-only status command is available while the browser process is running:

```sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer/analysis status
```

For embedding, import `AnalysisWorkspace` and `serve` from `stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace`. The controller exposes `register_source`, `save_query`, `saved_query`, `start`, `job`, `export_result`, `state` and `close`. `serve` returns the standard server, private control-file path and local capability URL. Call `server.server_close()` and `workspace.close()` after stopping the server; ordinary shutdown waits for its already dispatched analytical work.

The original standalone database API remains available. `DatasetDatabase.view_bindings()` returns the current view identities; pass that list as `expected_views` to `query` when a caller has reviewed them. `QueryResult.views` and `QueryResult.read_tables` identify the actual read transaction. `manifest_bytes(version_id)` returns the verified original manifest bytes, while the existing `manifest()` returns its parsed object.


## Use retained API responses in the same customer database

The **API responses** tab connects original JSON, CSV and typed stream results
to the existing Data, Changes, Analysis, Reports and Backup workflow. It reads
retained files; it does not send a provider request, create a quote, authorize
payment, finalize accounting, or acquire another page.

The local operator registers the original source before starting the server.
The browser uses that source's name and registration revision and never submits
a filesystem path. Use a distinct name for each response you want to retain.

### Register an original response

An existing SF88 buyer response uses the same original configuration and result
record that the original **read_retained_response()** accepts:

~~~sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer-analysis --checkout /private/stellar-forge \
  response --name regional_sales --input-kind buyer --format json \
  --config /private/buyer/config.json --result /private/buyer/result.json
~~~

For CSV, use **--format csv**. A standalone original SF31 response-file writer
can instead use **--input-kind sf31**: **--config** is its exact response-file
writer options object, including destination and maxBytes, and **--result**
is its returned SAVED receipt, including path, bytes and SHA-256. Both remain
private local files. An incomplete stream uses the original typed export
described below; a partial file is never relabeled SAVED by this command.

An original native MCP result keeps its original quote and invocation binding:

~~~sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer-analysis --checkout /private/stellar-forge \
  response --name paid_sales --input-kind mcp \
  --manifest /private/mcp-buyer/results/ORIGINAL_QUOTE_ID.meta.json
~~~

This calls the original McpResultStore in read-only mode and consumes its
original file(quote) / VerifiedFile interface. It opens no quote database
and makes no recovery or purchase call. The source manifest keeps the original
quote ID, invocation hash, native result classification and recorded payment
response. A server-confirmed payment remains that original classification; an
analytical import does not add a settlement or independently verify one.

An existing Python StreamDelivery needs no checkout or Node process:

~~~sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer-analysis \
  response --name game_records --input-kind stream \
  --stream-export /private/buyer/stream-exports/ORIGINAL_REQUEST_SHA
~~~

Register the complete original export directory containing manifest.json,
source.json and records.jsonl. This binds the original export request,
original response identity and completion state, then uses the original
StreamDelivery.records() reader. NDJSON values and SSE event framing stay
native. An export of valid events from an aborted response remains incomplete.

An unchanged registration is idempotent. Replacing a source alias requires its
current **--expected-revision**; previous response registrations remain retained
for the jobs that used them. Start the same server afterward:

~~~sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer-analysis --checkout /private/stellar-forge \
  serve --open
~~~

The existing source command with **--session** and **--room** remains unchanged.

### Choose the useful table

1. In **API responses**, select the registered source and choose **Inspect
   retained records**. The UI shows its native classification, format,
   response byte count, original SHA-256 and transport completion.
2. Select the record collection. JSON Pointer **/structuredContent/rows** selects
   rows from a native MCP structured result; **/rows** selects a root result's
   rows. An empty pointer selects the root array or one root object. CSV and
   typed stream exports already define their sequence of records.
3. Choose **Read fields from this collection** and edit the column mapping.
   A pointer such as **/players/white/rating** selects a nested scalar. For SSE,
   choose **Parse each data value as JSON** explicitly to use pointers such as
   **/data/meta/domain**; event ID, event type and original record index remain
   available alongside data.
4. Choose **Preview all mapped records**. The background action walks every
   retained row, verifies the selected fields and conversions, and retains the
   complete count and projected-byte digest. The displayed sample contains at
   most 25 rows and 256 KiB; it is labeled as a sample.
5. Review the source scope and choose **Import reviewed projection**. A native
   partial stream or a selected provider result marked **truncated: true**
   requires the visible incomplete-scope checkbox. The choice and original
   incomplete state remain in the imported manifest and report sources.
6. In **Data**, select the resulting immutable version for a SQL view, or use
   **Review changes** against an existing view first. Save SQL and assemble
   customer reports through the original tabs.

The importer does not assume that every JSON property is a row. It does not
silently flatten arrays, drop invalid rows, deduplicate records, normalize
currency strings, convert blank CSV fields to NULL, or infer that a missing
provider truncation flag proves an exhaustive provider result.

| Mapping type | Stored value |
| --- | --- |
| Native scalar | Original JSON scalar type; every CSV cell remains text. Numeric and exact decimal strings remain text. |
| Text | Strings stay exact; other scalar values become their JSON text representation. |
| Integer | An existing integer or canonical signed decimal text within SQLite's signed 64-bit range. No fractional truncation. |
| Number | Explicit conversion to a finite floating-point number; use Native or Text for exact decimal strings. |
| Boolean | JSON booleans or exact text true / false; stored as SQLite 1 / 0 with boolean provenance. |
| JSON text | Explicit canonical JSON representation for a selected object, array or scalar. |

JSON null remains SQL NULL for every mapping type. A missing pointer fails the
whole projection by default, identifying the original row and selected column.
Choosing **Use NULL** explicitly retains per-column missing-to-NULL counts.
Columns have no SQLite affinity, so later insertion does not silently coerce
numeric-looking text. Case-insensitive SQL column collisions are rejected.
CSV headers must be unique and every row must have the exact header width.

### Identity, review and recovery

The source is a hash-bound native response. The table is a derived analytical
projection with schema **stellar-forge.response-table-manifest.v1**. It is never
an SF100 delivery or merchant snapshot. Its manifest retains the original
response and input-file hashes, native source classification, precise mapping,
completion and provider declarations, missing-value policy, record count and
projected-row digest.

Preview and import are original durable workspace jobs. Import rereads the
original source, reconstructs the entire projection and requires the exact
reviewed preview hash. Changed bytes, metadata or mappings require another
preview. New jobs use the current registered source revision; repeating a
completed request ID returns that original job and never imports today's
replacement under an old review.

Both dataset-room imports and response projections use the same original
SQLite row transaction, scalar handling, immutable version identities and
view revision checks. A failed projection/import leaves previous tables and
selected views intact. Saved SQL results retain their actual source versions
from the same SQLite read snapshot. Reports retain these source identities and
completion scopes with their published rows; exports do not requery providers.

A database backup retains imported rows, exact analytical manifests,
registrations and their histories, previews/import jobs, saved SQL, comparisons,
report rows and publications. After restoring to a new private directory,
ordinary analysis and regenerated report exports work without wallet keys,
the original checkout or external response files. A new projection still needs
the corresponding original native files: configuration/result plus response
file, native MCP metadata/result, or all three original typed-export files.
Those external files are not copied into the database backup. Re-register a
moved source explicitly rather than editing historical paths or manifests.

Limits are explicit failures, never silent truncation: structured JSON is at
most 32 MiB; a retained input at most 256 MiB; a projection at most 1,000,000
rows, 128 MiB, 256 selected columns, 2 MiB per mapped row and 120 seconds.
Existing original readers can impose a stricter native file limit. Large
integers outside signed 64-bit range can be retained as Text; exact decimal
strings can remain Native text. The customer's selected provider-query scope
is distinct from transport completion and from analytical query row limits.

# Receive a complete Analysis workspace

An Analysis workspace archive contains the original consistent SQLite snapshot
and its complete retained query exports, report files, change outputs and
workbook editions. Receiving restores those files together into a new private
directory. The original workspace identity, dataset versions, jobs, saved
definitions and producer provenance remain in the copied database.

The receiver is part of the installed `stellar_forge_buyer` Python package. It
uses the existing public workbook receiver's private-file and atomic directory
publication helpers. Linux and macOS are supported when their native
no-replace directory rename is available.

## Review the selected archive

Keep the archive in a private directory with file permissions `0600`. Pass its
recorded SHA-256 when it is available:

```bash
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.workspace_archive_receive inspect \
  /private/customer/analysis-workspace.zip \
  --sha256 ARCHIVE_SHA256
```

The command streams and validates the exact archive through the maintained
`workspace_archive.inspect_archive` function. Its JSON result includes the
archive path, compressed byte count and digest, manifest digest, original
workspace ID, export job ID, complete file inventory and recorded table counts.
Review the original workspace identity and available payloads before selecting
the receiving destination.

`archive-manifest.json` is the root manifest. Each customer payload appears
under `workspace/` in the ZIP. Manifest `files` includes `datasets.sqlite3`
exactly once; `database` repeats that same path, byte count and digest. Prior
portable archives are recorded as provenance without nesting their contents.
The exporter retains the complete selected output trees and excludes process
launch capabilities, provider session directories, locks and temporary parts.

## Receive, then open the original application

Choose an absent destination below a private directory. The command can create
missing private parent directories. An existing destination remains intact.

```bash
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.workspace_archive_receive receive \
  /private/customer/analysis-workspace.zip \
  /private/customer/analysis-restored \
  --sha256 ARCHIVE_SHA256
```

The successful command prints one JSON receipt and exits with status `0`.
`target` identifies the new workspace directory and `database_path` identifies
its original `datasets.sqlite3`. Open that directory through the normal
application:

```bash
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer/analysis-restored status

python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer/analysis-restored serve --open
```

The normal application creates its current local serving capability and
performs its original interrupted-job reconciliation. An administrative export
job that was RUNNING in the consistent snapshot can therefore become
INTERRUPTED on first open. Existing business rows, complete output jobs,
workbook revisions and source identities retain their original history.
Existing source registrations preserve their producer provenance; additional
acquisition uses the application's normal explicit source configuration.

## Continue after an interruption

Repeat the same receive command with the same archive and destination. A
private journal beside the destination owns the operation and its staging.
Complete staged payloads are verified and reused. Incomplete members are
re-extracted from the original ZIP. The final directory appears atomically
after all members and the database pass validation.

| Retained phase | Continuation |
| --- | --- |
| `extracting` | Verify complete staged files, re-extract remaining members and inspect the immutable original database. |
| `prepared` | Verify the prepared directory and its receipt, then publish it with a native no-replace rename. |
| Rename completed before the journal update | Match the existing destination's retained directory identity and receipt, sync its parent directory and finish the original journal. |
| `complete` | Return the original receipt with `reused: true`, preserving later live database and application changes. |

The receiver validates the database with SQLite's immutable read-only mode,
its original application ID and schema version, the original Analysis
workspace ID, a full `quick_check`, required tables and recorded table counts.
It does not construct the application during extraction. Normal first open is
the application owner's existing recovery boundary.

An orchestrator can allocate and retain its operation UUID before dispatch:

```bash
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.workspace_archive_receive receive \
  /private/customer/analysis-workspace.zip \
  /private/customer/analysis-restored \
  --operation 1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef \
  --sha256 ARCHIVE_SHA256
```

Use that same UUID, archive and destination for every continuation of this
operation. Without `--operation`, the durable journal allocates a UUID once.
Keep the original ZIP and private journal available for subsequent receipt
readback. `workspace-archive-receipt.json` in the restored directory binds the
published workspace to that journal; the next exporter excludes this
receiver-generated metadata from its customer payload selection.

## Python interface and receipt

```python
from stellar_forge_buyer.workspace_archive import inspect_archive
from stellar_forge_buyer.workspace_archive_receive import restore_archive

review = inspect_archive(archive_path, expected_sha256=recorded_digest)
receipt = restore_archive(
    archive_path,
    new_directory,
    operation=retained_operation_id,
    expected_sha256=review["archive"]["sha256"],
)
```

`operation` and `expected_sha256` are optional. Operation IDs contain exactly
32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Digests contain 64 lowercase hexadecimal
characters. The receiving result uses
`stellar-forge.analysis-workspace-receipt.v1` and contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state`, `operation_id` | Completed receiving operation and its durable identity. |
| `archive_id`, `workspace_id` | Original export job and original customer workspace. |
| `archive_sha256`, `archive_bytes`, `manifest_sha256` | Exact selected source. |
| `target`, `database_path` | The selected receiving directory and its database. |
| `files`, `bytes` | Number of restored customer payloads and their total uncompressed size. |
| `created_at`, `prepared_at`, `completed_at` | Original receiving lifecycle timestamps. |
| `reused_staged_files` | Complete members retained at the successful preparation step. |
| `reused` | Whether this invocation continued or read back the retained operation. |

The saved receipt is stable across completed replay; the per-invocation
`reused` flag becomes `true`. The receiver checks its original archive and
publication identity during replay and preserves current customer file bytes.

## Operator errors

Successful CLI responses are JSON on stdout. Controlled failures are JSON on
stderr with exit status `2`; interruption exits `130`. A supplied operation
and the same destination allow the existing receiving to continue.

| Error suffix | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `TARGET_EXISTS` | Select an absent destination, or use the original archive and operation for that destination's completed receipt. |
| `OPERATION_CHANGED` | Reconcile the archive, destination and retained UUID against the original receiving request. |
| `STORAGE_REQUIRED` or `STORAGE_FULL` | Release space from completed owned work or provide capacity on the selected filesystem, then repeat the same command. |
| `ARCHIVE_CHANGED` or `MEMBER_CHANGED` | Recover the exact originally reviewed archive and repeat with its recorded digest. |
| `DATABASE_INVALID`, `DATABASE_IDENTITY_CHANGED` or `DATABASE_ROWS_CHANGED` | Return the exact source finding to the original exporter and correct the source archive before choosing a new receiving operation. |
| `STAGING_CHANGED` or `PUBLISHED_DIRECTORY_MISSING` | Inspect the original journal and selected directory; preserve their current contents while reconciling the changed local state. |
| `ATOMIC_PUBLICATION_UNAVAILABLE` | Use a supported Linux or macOS filesystem/runtime for the same source archive. |

Original private-storage, archive-inspection and operation-lock errors retain
their stable application codes. A busy receive can be read back by repeating
the same command after its original writer finishes.

# Export a complete customer SQL query

The analysis workspace's **Exports** tab runs a retained query review through
the original streaming `DatasetDatabase.export_query` engine and keeps its
complete files beside the analytical database. Use it to deliver a complete
query result after reviewing a smaller table in **Analysis**.

Start the existing workspace against the customer's database:

```sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace \
  --database /private/customer-analysis serve --open
```

Imported rows and retained analyses work without an acquisition checkout.
The launch URL comes from the existing private `analysis-launch.json`. The
server retains its loopback origin and capability access controls.

## Review, export, and download

1. Open **Analysis** and load a saved analysis or enter its SQL and parameter
   text. Choose the current data versions, then select **Review for full
   export**. An already completed analysis can instead use **Export every query
   row** from its result, or be selected in **Exports**.
2. Read the retained SQL, exact parameter text, preview count, reviewed views,
   and source context. The review is identified by its original job ID and
   result SHA-256. Changing a saved recipe does not change this review.
3. Select JSONL, CSV, SQLite, or a combination. All selected formats consume
   the same native query run and preserve its returned row order. Give the
   export a useful name.
4. Choose the execution timeout, which defaults to 300 seconds. Optional
   maximum row and combined output-byte limits are explicit failure limits.
   Leave them empty when the full SQL result should be exported. Exceeding
   either limit ends the job and retains its error in history.
5. Select **Export every query row**. The current rows and output bytes appear
   as the native writer reports progress. The query has no known percentage
   until it reaches completion. **Cancel export** records cancellation and
   signals the same running native query.
6. Open the completed result. Download each original file and `manifest.json`.
   The page includes the exact executed SQL and parameter text, original
   source scope, row count, file sizes, file hashes, and retained directory.
   **Newer exports** and **Older exports** page through the durable history.

The preview's row ceiling is separate from the export. For example, a review
that displays one of three rows exports all three when the SQL returns three
rows and no extra export ceiling is set. An explicit `LIMIT` in the SQL remains
part of the query and therefore also remains in the export.

The writer checks the original reviewed view bindings inside its own SQLite
read transaction. If a data view changed since the review, run a new review
against the intended versions. A completed export retains its original result
independently of subsequent view changes.

### Choose the file for its consumer

| File | Contents and use |
| --- | --- |
| `rows.jsonl` | One complete native JSON object per row. Integers and decimal strings retain their original values. Binary values and non-finite SQLite reals use the original typed encodings. Use `QueryExport.rows()` for Python values. |
| `rows.csv` | Ordinary CSV with a header. Spreadsheet-safe text is enabled by default and recorded in the manifest. Formula-like text gets an apostrophe prefix. NULL and empty text both appear as an empty CSV field; binary values use the documented `base64:` prefix. |
| `rows.sqlite3` | A portable SQLite database containing the `result` table. `_sf_export_row` preserves query order. Native values retain their SQLite storage types. |
| `manifest.json` | The original complete manifest: SQL and bindings, reviewed views, read tables, source versions, row count, and the bytes/SHA-256 of every selected output. |

Clear **Prepare CSV text for spreadsheet import** when the consumer needs
literal CSV text. JSONL and SQLite preserve typed values independently of this
CSV choice. Use a JSON reader that preserves signed 64-bit integers; JavaScript
number parsing can round them. The browser displays original parameter and
manifest text directly, and native downloads preserve the original bytes.

SQLite output requires unique column names, including case-insensitive
uniqueness, and reserves `_sf_export_row`. If the original engine returns
`QUERY_EXPORT_SQLITE_COLUMNS_REQUIRE_ALIASES`, add explicit aliases in the SQL,
run a new review, and export that review. The workspace preserves the original
column selection and names.

`queryComplete: true` means the selected SQL finished. The source versions can
still identify a partial acquired dataset, an acknowledged incomplete stream,
or a provider's limited query scope. Those original completion declarations
stay in `manifest.binding.sourceVersions` and in the browser's source details.

## Download large results and make a portable copy

The server enters the original `QueryExport.open()` context, verifies the full
chosen file, and sends success headers only after verification. It then streams
that same open descriptor in chunks, including its original SHA-256 header.
GET and HEAD use the same selected-file validation.

Native clients can continue an interrupted file with a single HTTP byte range.
Use the strong `ETag` from the original response as `If-Range` with, for example,
`Range: bytes=1048576-`. A matching validator returns the remaining bytes with
status 206 and an exact `Content-Range`; a changed validator returns the complete
file with status 200 so the client can replace its old partial copy. The ETag
and `X-Content-SHA256` always identify the entire immutable output. Validate the
whole received file against its manifest before publishing it for consumption.

The package includes a complete receiving client that performs this transfer,
resumes verified files and partial byte ranges, and reopens the original result
offline. Follow [Receive a complete customer query export](QUERY_EXPORT_DELIVERY.md)
for its CLI, Python API, progress, cancellation and portable recipient handover.

Browsers supporting streaming file save write directly to the chosen file.
The ordinary download fallback supports files up to 64 MiB. Larger files stay
complete at the displayed private directory and can use the existing native
copy command:

```sh
python -m stellar_forge_buyer.query_export inspect \
  --directory /private/customer-analysis/analysis-query-exports/EXPORT_JOB_ID

python -m stellar_forge_buyer.query_export copy \
  --directory /private/customer-analysis/analysis-query-exports/EXPORT_JOB_ID \
  --out /private/customer-handoff/export-edition-1
```

The parent of `--out` must already be private; the destination itself must be
new. Copy verifies and streams every selected output, then publishes the exact
original manifest bytes. The copied directory opens without the source
database, workspace process, provider session, checkout, or signing keys:

```python
from stellar_forge_buyer.query_export import QueryExport

result = QueryExport("/private/customer-handoff/export-edition-1")
manifest = result.inspect()
for row in result.rows():  # Requires JSONL among the selected outputs.
    consume(row)
```

Use `result.open("rows.sqlite3")` or `result.open("rows.csv")` as a context
manager when consuming those files. The descriptor belongs to that context.
`result.manifest` reads metadata; `result.inspect()` verifies every selected
output before returning the manifest.

## Cancellation, interruption, and reopen

The existing single workspace executor owns export dispatch. Progress and
cancellation use tiny private files under `analysis-query-exports/control`
outside the analytical SQLite database. The native query receives the same
process's `threading.Event.is_set` callback, avoiding a filesystem read for
every row or SQLite VM progress check.

Cancel ends an incomplete native export with status **CANCELLED**. An ordinary
failure retains **FAILED** and the original error code. Closing the workspace
signals pending and active exports before waiting for the original executor.
Progress retains observed row/byte counts and cancellation intent.

An abrupt process stop can leave an incomplete destination. Reopening marks
unfinished original jobs **INTERRUPTED**. An explicit retry uses a new request
ID and a fresh destination; the previous job and its incomplete directory remain
available for diagnosis. The native engine starts the complete query again for
that new attempt.

A process can stop after the native manifest is complete but before the job's
final database update. At reopen, the workspace inspects the original outputs,
checks their binding to the retained review, and adopts a valid complete export
as **COMPLETE**. It also reconciles that publication window after a late
callback or cancellation error. A valid published manifest wins over a late
cancellation request. This recovery reads the retained result and does not
dispatch the SQL again.

Keep the database directory and its `analysis-query-exports` directory together
to reopen the original export history and downloads. **Create database backup**
copies the analytical SQLite database, including export job records, but the
standalone export files live outside that backup. Use native `copy` for each
portable result you want to hand over. A restored database can review and export
its retained rows into a new local export directory.

## Use the same controller from Python

Close the browser server before opening another workspace job owner. The
original process lease prevents two executors from dispatching against one
database. This example takes an existing complete query review and starts an
export through the same path as the browser:

```python
import time
from uuid import uuid4
from stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_workspace import AnalysisWorkspace

workspace = AnalysisWorkspace("/private/customer-analysis")
try:
    review = workspace.job("ORIGINAL_COMPLETE_QUERY_JOB_ID")
    request = {
        "id": uuid4().hex,
        "query_id": review["id"],
        "result_sha256": review["result"]["result_sha256"],
        "label": "Operations export",
        "formats": ["jsonl", "csv", "sqlite"],
        "timeout": 300,
        "max_rows": None,
        "max_output_bytes": None,
        "spreadsheet_safe": True,
    }
    job = workspace.start("query-export", request)
    while job["status"] == "RUNNING":
        time.sleep(0.2)
        job = workspace.job(job["id"])
    if job["status"] != "COMPLETE":
        raise RuntimeError(job["error"] or job["status"])
    print(job["result"]["directory"])
finally:
    workspace.close()
```

Retry a response-lost start with the same original request ID and unchanged
content. That returns the existing job. Use a new ID for a deliberate new
attempt. `workspace.exports.cancel(job_id)` signals that original job;
`workspace.exports.history(before=sequence, limit=25)` reopens the paged history;
`workspace.exports.download(job_id, filename)` yields the verified descriptor
and recorded metadata in a context manager.

### Existing local HTTP surface

Requests use the launch capability in `X-Analysis-Capability` and the original
same-origin JSON request rules.

| Request | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/start/query-export` | Submit the same request object as the Python example through the original durable job owner. |
| `GET /api/jobs/<id>` | Read the original job, retained result, and observed export progress. |

                print(json.dumps(view.native, ensure_ascii=False))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run one explicitly selected original acquisition command."""
from dataclasses import asdict
import json
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import sys
import threading

from stellar_forge_buyer import AcquisitionWorkspace, AcquisitionError

if len(sys.argv) != 3:
    raise SystemExit("Usage: python acquisitions.py /absolute/sdk-settings.json /absolute/command.json")
workspace = AcquisitionWorkspace(**json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()))
request = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text())
command, p = request["command"], request.get("parameters", {})
cancel = threading.Event()
interrupted_exit = None


def interrupted(signum, _frame):
    global interrupted_exit
    interrupted_exit = interrupted_exit or 128 + signum
    cancel.set()


options = {"cancel_event": cancel}
actions = {
    "state": lambda: workspace.state(**options),
    "attach": lambda: workspace.attach_run(p["run"], **options),
    "request": lambda: workspace.request(p["id"], **options),
    "receive": lambda: workspace.receive_request(p["file"], filename=p.get("filename"), **options),
    "review-request": lambda: workspace.review_request(p["id"], accept_index=p["acceptIndex"],
        total_atomic=p["totalAtomic"], daily_atomic=p["dailyAtomic"], **options),
    "prepare-request": lambda: workspace.prepare_request(p["id"], review_sha256=p["reviewSha256"], **options),
    "paid-file": lambda: workspace.paid_file(p["id"], **options),
    "receive-paid-file": lambda: workspace.receive_paid_file(p["file"], filename=p.get("filename"), **options),
    "review-paid-file": lambda: workspace.review_paid_file(p["id"], expected_revision=p["expectedRevision"],
        total_atomic=p["totalAtomic"], daily_atomic=p["dailyAtomic"], filename=p["filename"],
        claim_env=p["claimEnv"], **options),
    "prepare-paid-file": lambda: workspace.prepare_paid_file(p["id"], review_sha256=p["reviewSha256"], **options),
    "retrieve-paid-file": lambda: workspace.retrieve_paid_file(p["id"], only=p["only"],
        config_sha256=p["configSha256"], handoff_sha256=p["handoffSha256"], **options),
    "reset-paid-file": lambda: workspace.reset_paid_file(p["id"], only=p["only"],
        config_sha256=p["configSha256"], handoff_sha256=p["handoffSha256"], **options),
    "download-paid-file": lambda: workspace.download_paid_file(p["id"], p["operationId"], p["destination"], **options),
    "export-paid-file": lambda: workspace.export_paid_file(p["id"], destination=p["destination"], **options),
    "draft": lambda: workspace.draft(p["id"], revision=p.get("revision"), **options),
    "save": lambda: workspace.save(p["manifest"], acquisition_id=p.get("id"),
        expected_revision=p.get("expectedRevision", 0), **options),
    "initialize": lambda: workspace.initialize(p["id"], expected_revision=p["expectedRevision"],
        review_sha256=p["reviewSha256"], **options),
    "inspect": lambda: workspace.inspect(p["id"], **options),
    "execute": lambda: workspace.execute(p["id"], expected_plan_sha256=p["expectedPlanSha256"],
        only=p.get("only"), **options),
    "recover": lambda: workspace.recover(p["id"], **options),
    "unlock": lambda: workspace.unlock(p["id"], owner_pid=p["ownerPid"], **options),
    "finalize": lambda: workspace.finalize(p["id"], only=p.get("only"), **options),
    "bind-accounting": lambda: workspace.bind_accounting(p["id"], only=p["only"],
        workspace=p["workspace"], **options),
    "preview": lambda: workspace.preview(p["id"], p["operationId"], **options),
    "download": lambda: workspace.download(p["id"], p["operationId"], p["destination"], **options),
    "export": lambda: workspace.export(p["id"], format=p["format"], destination=p["destination"], **options),
    "export-request": lambda: workspace.export_request(p["id"], kind=p["kind"],
        destination=p["destination"], **options),
    "backup-review": lambda: workspace.backup_review(state_root=p["stateRoot"], **options),
    "backup": lambda: workspace.backup(state_root=p["stateRoot"], output=p["output"],
        review_sha256=p["reviewSha256"], quiesced=p["quiesced"],
        passphrase_env=p.get("passphraseEnv"), **options),
    "verify": lambda: workspace.verify(bundle=p["bundle"],
        expected_record_sha256=p.get("expectedRecordSha256"), passphrase_env=p.get("passphraseEnv"),
        python=p.get("python"), **options),
    "restore": lambda: workspace.restore(bundle=p["bundle"],
        expected_record_sha256=p.get("expectedRecordSha256"), passphrase_env=p.get("passphraseEnv"),
        python=p.get("python"), **options),
}
if command not in actions:
    raise SystemExit("Choose one command: " + ", ".join(actions))
previous = {sig: signal.signal(sig, interrupted) for sig in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM)}
try:
    result = actions[command]()
    print(json.dumps(asdict(result), indent=2))
except AcquisitionError as error:
    print(json.dumps({"code": error.code, "result": asdict(error.result)}, indent=2))
    raise SystemExit(interrupted_exit or 2)
finally:
    for sig, handler in previous.items():
        signal.signal(sig, handler)

"""Run an existing original Buyer intent through a persistent agent customer.

Install the original package with its [agents] extra. Prepare the request with
Buyer.prepare/from_workspace/from_paid_file first, retaining its stable intent.
This host can be restarted with the same --state and --run values.
"""
import argparse
import json

from stellar_forge_buyer import Buyer
from stellar_forge_buyer.agent_workflow import CustomerWorkflow
from stellar_forge_buyer.agent_tools import create_tools


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--checkout", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--intent", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--run", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--format", choices=("auto", "json", "csv", "binary", "sse", "ndjson", "paid-file"), default="auto")
    parser.add_argument("--allow-partial", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--action", choices=("execute", "recover", "review", "cancel"))
    parser.add_argument("--review-key")
    parser.add_argument("--offset", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=20)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    buyer = Buyer(checkout=args.checkout, state_dir=args.state, timeout=360)
    with CustomerWorkflow(buyer) as customer:
        customer.register(args.run, intent_id=args.intent, format=args.format,
                          allow_partial=args.allow_partial)
        state = customer.start(args.run)
        if args.action:
            state = customer.resume(args.run, action=args.action, review_key=args.review_key)
        if state["status"] != "AVAILABLE":
            print(json.dumps(state, indent=2))
            return
        tools = {tool.name: tool for tool in create_tools(customer)}
        # This same ToolCall shape is emitted by an existing LangChain agent.
        message = tools["stellar_forge_read"].invoke({
            "name": "stellar_forge_read", "type": "tool_call", "id": args.run + "-page",
            "args": {"run_id": args.run, "offset": args.offset, "limit": args.limit},
        })
        handoff = customer.export(args.run)
        print(json.dumps({"run": state, "model_content": message.content,
                          "page": message.artifact, "handoff": {
                              "directory": handoff["directory"],
                              "manifest_sha256": handoff["manifest_sha256"],
                              "complete": handoff["complete"], "reused": handoff["reused"]}}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Use an existing merchant handoff and original workspace from a Python app.

Preparation, purchase, download and consumption are separate explicit actions.
The merchant file must already have been enrolled with original checkout.mjs.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys

from stellar_forge_buyer import Buyer, BuyerError, DeliveryError


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("action", choices=["prepare", "review", "purchase", "download", "transfer", "reset-transfer", "consume", "finalize", "history"])
    parser.add_argument("--checkout", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--intent", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--workspace")
    parser.add_argument("--handoff")
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout-ms", type=int, default=30000)
    parser.add_argument("--resume", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    buyer = Buyer(checkout=args.checkout, state_dir=args.state)
    if args.action == "prepare":
        if not args.workspace or not args.handoff:
            parser.error("prepare requires --workspace and --handoff")
        operation = buyer.from_paid_file(args.handoff, workspace=args.workspace, intent_id=args.intent)
    else:
        operation = buyer.operation(args.intent)
    if args.action in ("prepare", "review", "purchase"):
        review = operation.review()
        print(json.dumps({"originalReview": review.native, "filePromise": review.file_promise,
                          "workspace": review.workspace_directory}, indent=2))
        if args.action == "purchase":
            result = operation.execute(review=review)
            print(json.dumps(result.record, indent=2))
            return 0 if result.ok else 2
    elif args.action == "download":
        delivery = operation.retrieve_file(destination=args.out, timeout_ms=args.timeout_ms, resume=args.resume)
        print(json.dumps(delivery.record, indent=2))
    elif args.action == "transfer":
        print(json.dumps(operation.inspect_file_transfer(destination=args.out).record, indent=2))
    elif args.action == "reset-transfer":
        print(json.dumps(operation.reset_file_transfer(destination=args.out).record, indent=2))
    elif args.action == "finalize":
        accounting = operation.finalize()
        print(json.dumps(accounting.record, indent=2))
        return 0 if accounting.finalized else 2
    elif args.action == "history":
        print(json.dumps(operation.inspect(), indent=2))
    else:
        delivery = operation.recover_file()
        if delivery is None:
            print(json.dumps(operation.inspect(), indent=2))
            return 2
        # Consume the merchant's actual CSV through the verified same descriptor.
        # Replace this accumulation with the application's own import operation.
        count, columns = 0, None
        for row in delivery.csv_rows():
            count += 1
            if columns is None:
                columns = list(row)
        print(json.dumps({"rows": count, "columns": columns or [],
            "sourceSha256": delivery.delivery["sha256"], "sourceBytes": delivery.delivery["bytes"],
            "localConsumption": True}))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except BuyerError as error:
        result = {"error": error.code, "operationDirectory":
            str(error.operation.directory) if error.operation else None}
        if isinstance(error, DeliveryError):
            result.update(retainedBytes=error.retained_bytes, resumable=error.resumable,
                partialPath=error.partial_path, transferState=error.transfer_state_path)
        print(json.dumps(result), file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)

"""Complete existing DBnomics source -> Analysis -> workbook -> reviewed return.

Run this against the already completed native DBnomics receiving project.
No new provider capture or purchase is requested. An optional real analyst note
is written to one explicitly selected observation, then reviewed and adopted.
